## Scope and status {#sec-cov-scope}

This chapter estimates, for each scored cell type $j$ at each
bulk-matched time, the mean $\widehat{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_{\cdot j}$ and
the within-type covariance $\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}_{j}$ of the
gene panel of tier (ii) (@sec-fs-consistency), and exports them on the
linear scale of DeCovarT's convolution,

$$
\bigl\{
\widehat{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_{\cdot j},\,
\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}_{j},\,
\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Omega}}_{j}=\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}_{j}^{-1}
\bigr\}_{j=1}^{J},
\qquad
\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}_{j}\succ 0 .
$$ {#eq-grn-export}

The target is the covariance that enters the likelihood, not a
mechanistic gene network; a dense estimate is therefore an acceptable
plug-in
([3.2, why a regularised covariance](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-2-covariance-network-estimation.html#nte-cov-why)).

**Plug-in and sensitivity analyses.** The exported plug-in is the
shrinkage covariance (@sec-shrinkage). Four arms are sensitivity
analyses of that choice: the graphical lasso (@sec-glasso), the
`SILGGM` support with a refit (@sec-silggm), `PLNnetwork` (@sec-pln)
and the shrinkage of the denoised covariance (@sec-cov-denoised). All
five are scored by the same nested cross-validation (@sec-cov-cv-run);
their theory is summarised in
[3.2, estimators](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-2-covariance-network-estimation.html#tbl-cov-estimators).

| Item | Code | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Panel input | `R/cv_covariance_selection.R`: `read_panel_slot()` | written, not run |
| Five arms, one fit wrapper per estimator | same file: `fit_cov_shrinkage()`, `fit_cov_glasso()`, `fit_cov_silggm_refit()`, `fit_cov_plnnetwork()`; `preprocess = "denoised"` for the first three | written, not run |
| Denoising and extrinsic noise | same file: `denoise_covariance()`, `reconstruct_count_covariance()`, `extrinsic_noise_nu()`; `pln_linear_moments(size_term, poisson_diag)` | written, not run |
| Held-out score, tuning, nested comparison | same file: `heldout_gaussian_logscore()`, `score_fit()`, `cv_select_tuning()`, `nested_cv_compare()` | written, not run |
| Driver for the five arms | `scripts/03_04_cv_covariance.R` | written, not run |
| Graphical lasso EBIC path (diagnostic) | `scripts/03_01_grn_glasso.R`, `R/ebic_regularisation_path.R` | input moved to the gated panel; not re-run |
| `SILGGM` fit | `scripts/03_02_grn_silggm.R` | input moved to the gated panel; never run |

### Inputs and scales {#sec-cov-inputs}

Every arm reads the raw UMI counts of the scored cells, element
`slots[[time]]` of `output/feature_selection/tier_01/scored_slots.rds`
(@sec-fs-qc-applied): `counts` (genes × cells), `cell_type`, `batch`
and `library_size`, the full RNA library of each cell. The counts are
restricted to the genes of
`output/feature_selection/tier_02/selected_<time>.csv`, the panel gated
by the permuted Welch $G$ at BH 0.05 (@sec-fs-consistency): 1,417 genes
at 48 h, 3,420 at 72 h and 5,821 at 96 h, with no cap.
`read_panel_slot()` does the subset and returns cells × genes. The
500-gene legacy export of @sec-fs-export is no longer read. A
transformation belongs to one arm only.

**Normalisation.** The exported means and covariances are computed on
raw per-cell UMI counts, with no per-cell library division
(`normalise = "none"`). Dividing each cell by its total library removes
the type-level transcriptome size $S_j$: signatures become mRNA
fractions, and the proportions are estimated as
$q_j\propto p_jS_j$ instead of $p_j$
[@luTranscriptomeSizeMatters2025]. It also removes the biological size
variation between cells of one type, which the bulk accumulates.
Without spike-ins the technical size factor cannot be separated from
the biological one, so the size term of the covariance is bracketed by
the coefficient $\kappa$ of the denoised estimator (@sec-cov-denoised):
$\kappa=0$ treats all size variation as biological;
$\kappa=\hat\nu/(1+\hat\nu)$ treats it all as technical, which matches
library normalisation for the covariance. The argument is in
[3.2, raw or denoised](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-2-covariance-network-estimation.html#sec-raw-vs-denoised).
The earlier per-cell division, `X <- y / (lib / ref_lib)` with
`ref_lib` the median library of the time point, is kept only as a
sensitivity variant (`normalise = "library"`). `PLNnetwork` keeps its
full-library offset $\log s_c$ in both cases.

| Arm | What is passed in | Scale of the export |
|---|---|---|
| Shrinkage (`corpcor`), plug-in | raw per-cell UMI counts | linear, raw counts |
| Graphical lasso (`glasso`) | correlation matrix of the same counts | linear, after rescaling by the sample standard deviations |
| `SILGGM` | nonparanormal scores, for the support only | linear, refit under the support |
| `PLNnetwork` | raw UMI counts, offset $\log s_c$ (full library) | linear, through the moment map of @sec-pln; the two denoised brackets are exported beside it |
| Denoised shrinkage, $\kappa=0$ | raw counts, @eq-cov-denoised with $\kappa=0$ (Poisson diagonal removed), eigenvalues clipped at zero | $\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}^{\mathrm{bio}}_{j}$; scored through @eq-cov-renoise |
| Denoised shrinkage, $\kappa=\hat\kappa_{\max}$ (variant) | raw counts, @eq-cov-denoised with $\kappa=\hat\nu/(1+\hat\nu)$, eigenvalues clipped at zero | $\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}^{\mathrm{bio}}_{j}$; tuned by cross-validation, outside the nested comparison |
| Library-divided counts (variant, `normalise = "library"`) | `y / (lib / ref_lib)` for the first four arms; the denoised arm is left out | linear, library-divided counts |

: What each arm sees and what it exports. The first row is the plug-in. {#tbl-cov-inputs}

Earlier choices reverted, in code that has not been re-run:

- **Scale of the export.** `scripts/03_01_grn_glasso.R` (then named
  `03_01_grn_huge.R`) used to fit and export on $\log(1+x)$
  (`x <- log1p(x)`, then `mu <- colMeans(x)`). The convolution is
  linear only on an additive scale
  ([2.1, normalisation](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/02-1-single-cell-generative-optimisation.html#sec-norm-linear)),
  so $\widehat{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_{\cdot j}$ and
  $\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}_{j}$ are now computed on the linear
  counts. A $\log(1+x)$ table may still be used to detect a support,
  never to export a moment.
- **Per-cell library division.** `scripts/03_04_cv_covariance.R`
  divided each cell by its library (`X <- y / (lib / ref_lib)`), which
  is option (b) of
  [3.2, raw or denoised](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-2-covariance-network-estimation.html#sec-raw-vs-denoised).
  It is now the `normalise = "library"` variant.

### Units and regimes {#sec-cov-units}

Each fit uses the cells of one type at one time, treated as
independent draws: eleven type × time units (@tbl-fs-cell-counts).
Cell line is not a covariate (@sec-geo-design). The panel has $G_t$
genes at time $t$, before genes constant within a type are removed.
@tbl-cov-units sets the $C_j$ cells of each unit against three
sample-size layers
([3.2, regimes](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-2-covariance-network-estimation.html#sec-cov-regimes)):
existence of the maximum-likelihood estimate of
$\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{j}$, support recovery by the graphical lasso, and
support recovery by neighbourhood selection.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-cov-units
#| tbl-cap: "The eleven type × time units against the gated panel. $C_j$: scored cells of the unit (`cell_counts.csv`); $G_t$: panel genes at that time (rows of `selected_<time>.csv`). The two recovery columns are orders of magnitude without their constants, with natural logarithms and an assumed maximum node degree $d=10$ of the precision graph; they are not thresholds. Shaded rows ($C_j\\le G_t$) have a singular sample covariance and need a regularised estimate."
#| echo: false
fs_dir <- here::here("..", "output", "feature_selection")
units <- utils::read.csv(
  file.path(fs_dir, "tier_01", "cell_counts.csv"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
  fileEncoding = "UTF-8"
)
units <- units[units$scored, , drop = FALSE]
units <- units[order(units$time_point, -units$cells), , drop = FALSE]
times <- unique(units$time_point)
panel_size <- vapply(
  times,
  function(tm) {
    nrow(utils::read.csv(
      file.path(fs_dir, "tier_02", paste0("selected_", tm, ".csv")),
      fileEncoding = "UTF-8"
    ))
  },
  integer(1)
)
d <- 10 # assumed maximum degree of the precision graph
g <- unname(panel_size[units$time_point])
glasso_order <- d^2 * log(g)
neighbour_order <- d * log(g)
fmt <- function(x) format(round(x), big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)
yes_no <- function(x) ifelse(x, "yes", "no")
tab <- data.frame(
  sub("h$", " h", units$time_point),
  units$cell_type,
  fmt(units$cells),
  fmt(g),
  yes_no(units$cells >= g + 1),
  fmt(glasso_order),
  yes_no(units$cells > glasso_order),
  fmt(neighbour_order),
  yes_no(units$cells > neighbour_order)
)
colnames(tab) <- c(
  "Time",
  "Cell type",
  "$C_j$",
  "$G_t$",
  "MLE of $\\boldsymbol{\\Sigma}_j$ exists ($C_j\\ge G_t+1$)",
  "$d^{2}\\log G_t$",
  "$C_j>d^{2}\\log G_t$",
  "$d\\log G_t$",
  "$C_j>d\\log G_t$"
)
singular <- which(units$cells <= g)
tinytable::tt(tab) |>
  tinytable::group_tt(
    j = list(
      "Graphical-lasso support recovery" = 6:7,
      "Neighbourhood selection" = 8:9
    )
  ) |>
  tinytable::format_tt(i = 0, quarto = TRUE) |>
  tinytable::style_tt(j = c(3, 4, 6, 8), align = "r") |>
  tinytable::style_tt(i = singular, background = "#fbe3d6")
```

In nine of the eleven units $C_j\le G_t$: the sample covariance is
singular, and only a regularised estimate exists. Only the 48 h
epiblast (10,590 cells against 1,417 genes) and the 72 h primitive
streak (4,279 against 3,420) have a maximum-likelihood estimate. Four
units exceed the graphical-lasso order and eight the
neighbourhood-selection order; the 48 h and 72 h naïve pluripotency and
the somite differentiation front exceed neither. The cross-validated
score of @sec-cov-cv-run is defined in every regime because each arm
returns a positive definite matrix.

### Bulk depth per cell {#sec-cov-bulk-depth}

Which covariance enters the bulk law, raw or denoised, depends on the
bulk depth per cell relative to the reference
([3.2, raw or denoised](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-2-covariance-network-estimation.html#sec-raw-vs-denoised)):
the raw covariance is exact only at $a_i=1$. For bulk sample $i$,

$$
a_i=\frac{y_{+i}/n_i}{\bar s_{\mathrm{ref}}},
$$ {#eq-cov-bulk-depth}

<!-- chk: V45 -->

with $y_{+i}$ the total counts of the bulk sample, $n_i$ the number of
cells in it, and $\bar s_{\mathrm{ref}}$ the median UMIs per reference
cell at the matched time. $a_i<1$ is expected: the bulk library is
deeper in total than one droplet, but it spreads that depth over every
cell of the pooled sample. Bulk counts are reads, not UMIs, so their
sampling noise is overdispersed, with a dispersion $\omega_i\ge1$ that
lowers the effective depth to $a_i/\omega_i$. The raw plug-in, the
implemented default, assumes $a_i=1$. $n_i$ is
[TODO: cells per gastruloid × gastruloids per bulk sample, from the Suppinger et al. 2023 methods]{.highlight}
[@suppingerMultimodalCharacterizationMurine2023].

```{r}
#| label: cov-bulk-depth-call
#| eval: false
# Not run. Bulk depth per cell a_i of the standard-Wnt samples
# (GSE229386) against the scored reference cells of the matched time.
source("R/02_00_utils.R")
source("R/02_01_stats_quality_control.R")
htseq <- read_bulk_htseq(
  "data/raw/GSE229386_AllHTSeqCountsWithGeneNames.txt.gz"
)
# HTSeq summary rows (__no_feature, __ambiguous, ...) are not genes.
is_gene <- !startsWith(rownames(htseq$counts), "__")
slots <- readRDS("output/feature_selection/tier_01/scored_slots.rds")
# TODO: cells per gastruloid x gastruloids per bulk sample, from the
# Suppinger et al. 2023 methods.
cells_per_bulk <- NA_real_
bulk_depth <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(c("48h", "72h", "96h"), function(tm) {
    samples <- standard_wnt_samples(colnames(htseq$counts), tm)
    y_total <- colSums(htseq$counts[is_gene, samples, drop = FALSE])
    s_ref <- stats::median(slots$slots[[tm]]$library_size)
    data.frame(
      time_point = tm,
      sample = samples,
      bulk_counts = y_total,
      ref_median_umi = s_ref,
      a = (y_total / cells_per_bulk) / s_ref
    )
  })
)
```

## Estimators as run {#sec-cov-estimators}

None of the five arms penalises the diagonal: the three sparse
estimators leave the diagonal of the precision unpenalised, and the
shrinkage target D keeps the variances. Why the diagonal must not be
penalised is in
[3.2, diagonal](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-2-covariance-network-estimation.html#sec-cov-diagonal).
Each arm has exactly one tuning parameter, chosen by @sec-cov-cv-run.

| Arm | Wrapper | Underlying call | Tuning parameter | Grid |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Shrinkage (plug-in) | `fit_cov_shrinkage()` | `corpcor::cov.shrink(x, lambda, lambda.var = 0)` | intensity $\lambda\in[0,1]$ | around the closed-form $\hat\lambda^{\ast}$ |
| Graphical lasso | `fit_cov_glasso()` | `glasso::glasso(R, rho = lambda, penalize.diagonal = FALSE)` | $\lambda$ | log-spaced between $\lambda_{\min}$ and $\lambda_{\max}$ |
| `SILGGM` refit | `fit_cov_silggm_refit()` | `SILGGM::SILGGM(npn, method = "D-S_GL", global = TRUE, alpha)`, then `glasso::glasso(..., zero = ...)` | FDR level $\alpha$ | a short grid containing 0.05 |
| `PLNnetwork` | `fit_cov_plnnetwork()` | `PLNmodels::PLNnetwork(Abundance ~ 1 + offset(log_library), control = PLNnetwork_param(...))` | penalty | the family's own penalty grid |
| Denoised shrinkage | `fit_cov_shrinkage(preprocess = "denoised", kappa)` | `denoise_covariance(x, kappa)`, then target D on the denoised variances | intensity $\lambda$; $\kappa$ bracketed, not tuned | the shrinkage grid |

: The five arms, their calls and their tuning parameter. The first row is the plug-in; the other four are sensitivity analyses. The grids are set in `scripts/03_04_cv_covariance.R`. {#tbl-cov-estimators}

### Shrinkage covariance {#sec-shrinkage}

`fit_cov_shrinkage()` calls `corpcor::cov.shrink()` [@R-corpcor] with
the Schäfer–Strimmer target D: variances kept, correlations shrunk
towards zero by a common factor
[@schäferShrinkageApproachLargescale2005]. `corpcor` 1.6.10 also
shrinks the variances towards their median by default;
`lambda.var = 0` switches that off, so the target is exactly D. The
closed-form intensity $\hat\lambda^{\ast}$ (`corpcor::estimate.lambda()`)
is the centre of the grid, and cross-validation picks the value used.
The estimate is positive definite for any $C_j$ and $G_t$, so it is the
plug-in, and the estimator used when the others fail. The theory is in
[3.2, shrinkage](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-2-covariance-network-estimation.html#sec-cov-shrinkage).

### Denoised shrinkage {#sec-cov-denoised}

`fit_cov_shrinkage(preprocess = "denoised", kappa)` applies the moment
correction of
[3.2, raw or denoised](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-2-covariance-network-estimation.html#sec-raw-vs-denoised)
before the shrinkage. With $\boldsymbol{V}_j$ the unbiased sample
covariance of the raw counts of the $C_j$ cells and
$\bar{\boldsymbol{x}}_j$ their mean (`denoise_covariance()`),

$$
\widetilde{\boldsymbol{V}}_j
=
\boldsymbol{V}_j-\operatorname{diag}(\bar{\boldsymbol{x}}_j)
-\kappa\Bigl[\boldsymbol{V}_j-\operatorname{diag}(\bar{\boldsymbol{x}}_j)
+\bar{\boldsymbol{x}}_j\bar{\boldsymbol{x}}_j^{\top}
-\frac{\boldsymbol{V}_j}{C_j}\Bigr].
$$ {#eq-cov-denoised}

<!-- chk: V38b, V14a, V14b, V14c, V14e -->

1. The eigenvalues of $\widetilde{\boldsymbol{V}}_j$ below zero are
   raised to zero, the nearest positive semi-definite matrix in
   Frobenius norm
   [TODO-cite: Datta & Zou 2017 (CoCoLasso); Loh & Wainwright 2012; keys not in bibliography/REFERENCES.bib]{.highlight}.
   This costs one eigen-decomposition of a $G_t\times G_t$ matrix per
   training set.
2. A gene whose denoised variance is not positive is a Poisson gene at
   this depth. Its variance is floored at $10^{-4}$ times the median
   positive denoised variance, its correlations are set to zero, and it
   is listed in `floored_genes`.
3. Target D is applied to the projected matrix:
   $\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}^{\mathrm{bio}}_{j}=\boldsymbol{D}^{1/2}\{(1-\lambda)\boldsymbol{R}+\lambda\boldsymbol{I}\}\boldsymbol{D}^{1/2}$,
   with $\boldsymbol{R}$ and $\boldsymbol{D}$ its correlation and
   variances, and $\lambda$ chosen on the grid of @sec-shrinkage.

The exported matrix is $\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}^{\mathrm{bio}}_{j}$.
The held-out cells are raw counts and carry the Poisson noise and the
size term that the correction removed, so the arm is scored through the
raw count covariance rebuilt from the estimate, with
$\nu^{\mathrm{tech}}=\kappa/(1-\kappa)$:

$$
\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}^{\mathrm{score}}_{j}
=
\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}^{\mathrm{bio}}_{j}
+\operatorname{diag}(\widehat{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_{\cdot j})
+\frac{\kappa}{1-\kappa}
\bigl(\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}^{\mathrm{bio}}_{j}
+\widehat{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_{\cdot j}\widehat{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_{\cdot j}^{\top}\bigr)
$$ {#eq-cov-renoise}

<!-- chk: V38c -->

(`reconstruct_count_covariance()`, element `score_sigma` of the fit,
used by `score_fit()` when present). With $\kappa=0$ it is
$\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}^{\mathrm{bio}}_{j}+\operatorname{diag}(\widehat{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_{\cdot j})$.
The cross-validation therefore compares only how the biological part is
regularised; it cannot choose $\kappa$, because every $\kappa$ rebuilds
the same raw moments up to regularisation. $\kappa$ stays a bracket:
the nested comparison uses $\kappa=0$, which needs no estimate, and the
upper end $\hat\kappa_{\max}=\hat\nu/(1+\hat\nu)$ is exported as a
variant (`shrinkage_denoised_kappa_max`), tuned but not compared.

$\hat\nu$ comes from `extrinsic_noise_nu()`: the mode of the normalised
covariances $\widehat{\operatorname{Cov}}(x_g,x_h)/(\bar x_g\bar x_h)$
over pairs of genes with a mean of at least one count (at most 2,000
genes, largest means first), after Fang and Pachter
[TODO-cite: Fang & Pachter 2025, extrinsic biological stochasticity; key fangExtrinsicBiologicalStochasticity2025 is in the DeCovarT bibliography, not in bibliography/REFERENCES.bib]{.highlight}.
The estimate assumes that most gene pairs are intrinsically
uncorrelated; co-regulated modules bias $\hat\nu$ upwards. Without
spike-ins $\hat\nu$ mixes the biological and technical size factors,
so $\hat\kappa_{\max}$ is the all-technical end of the bracket. The
estimates are written per unit to `output/grn/cv/extrinsic_noise.csv`.

The graphical lasso and the `SILGGM` refit accept the same
preprocessing (`preprocess = "denoised"`). The graphical lasso then
fits the correlation of the projected matrix. For `SILGGM`, ranks
cannot be denoised: the support still comes from the nonparanormal
scores, and only the linear-scale refit on that support uses the
projected matrix. Neither variant is an arm of the nested comparison.

### Graphical lasso with an unpenalised diagonal {#sec-glasso}

`fit_cov_glasso()` standardises the panel, fits
`glasso::glasso(R, rho = lambda, penalize.diagonal = FALSE)` [@R-glasso]
on the sample correlation $\boldsymbol{R}_j$ by block coordinate
descent [@friedmanSparseInverseCovariance2008], and rescales:
$\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Omega}}_{j}=\Delta_j^{-1/2}\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Omega}}_{R}\Delta_j^{-1/2}$
with $\Delta_j=\operatorname{diag}(\boldsymbol{V}_j)$
(`rescale_correlation_fit()`). With the diagonal unpenalised the fitted
correlation keeps a unit diagonal, so $\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}_{j}$
matches the sample variances.

- `penalize.diagonal` defaults to `TRUE` in `glasso` 1.11; it is set
  explicitly.
- `huge` [@R-huge] is not used: `huge.glasso()` always penalises the
  diagonal and has no switch for it (checked in the `huge` 1.5.1
  sources). The reasons are in
  [3.2, graphical lasso](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-2-covariance-network-estimation.html#sec-cov-glasso).
- Grid endpoints come from `lambda_endpoints()`: at
  $\lambda_{\max}=\max_{g\neq g'}|R_{gg'}|$ the off-diagonal precision
  is zero; the lower end is of order $\sqrt{\log G_t/C_j}$.
- A gene constant across the cells of a type is left out of that
  type's fit and listed in `excluded_genes`, instead of forcing a
  diagonal covariance for all genes.
- A penalty whose solve fails is dropped from the grid and listed in
  `failed_lambda`, instead of being replaced by a diagonal precision.

The earlier selector, a safeguarded EBIC interval search
(`ebic_adaptive_path()`, at most `n_solves = 40` solves,
$\gamma=0.5$ [@foygelExtendedBayesianInformation2010]), is kept in
`scripts/03_01_grn_glasso.R` as a diagnostic path. It no longer chooses
$\lambda$.

### `SILGGM` support, then a refit {#sec-silggm}

`fit_cov_silggm_refit()` runs in three steps:

1. Nonparanormal scores with `huge::huge.npn(x, npn.func = "shrinkage")`
   (rank $R_{gc}$ mapped to $\Phi^{-1}\{R_{gc}/(C_j+1)\}$, then
   standardised). The choice of shrinkage over truncation is argued in
   [3.2, nonparanormal](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-2-covariance-network-estimation.html#sec-cov-npn).
2. `SILGGM::SILGGM(npn, method = "D-S_GL", global = TRUE, alpha)`
   [@R-SILGGM; @zhangSILGGMExtensivePackage2018]: de-sparsified
   graphical lasso with the global FDR rule of
   @liuGaussianGraphicalModel2013. The object kept is the support at
   level $\alpha$ (`global_decision`), not the dense de-sparsified
   matrix.
3. An SPD refit on the linear-scale panel under the zeros of that
   support, with `glasso::glasso(V, rho = 0, zero = ..., penalize.diagonal = FALSE)`;
   with `preprocess = "denoised"`, on the projected denoised matrix of
   @sec-cov-denoised.

The script `scripts/03_02_grn_silggm.R` (seed 1, $\alpha=0.05$) stops
after step 2 and has never been run; the refit lives in the wrapper.

### `PLNnetwork` {#sec-pln}

`fit_cov_plnnetwork()` fits the Poisson-lognormal network of `PLNmodels`
[@R-PLNmodels; @chiquetVariationalInferenceSparse2018] to the raw
counts of one unit, with the full-library offset:

$$
x_{gc}\mid\boldsymbol{z}_{\cdot c}
\sim
\mathrm{Poisson}\bigl(s_{c}\,e^{z_{gc}}\bigr),
\qquad
\boldsymbol{z}_{\cdot c}
\sim
\mathcal{N}_{G}(\boldsymbol{\mu}_{z},\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{z}),
\qquad
\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{z}=\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{z}^{-1}\ \text{penalised off the diagonal}.
$$ {#eq-pln}

| Argument | Value |
|---|---|
| formula | `Abundance ~ 1 + offset(log_library)`, one fit per unit, no further design |
| `log_library` | $\log s_c$, full RNA library (`library_size` of the slot, @sec-cov-inputs) |
| `n_penalties` | 40 |
| `min_ratio` | 0.1 |
| `penalize_diagonal` | `FALSE` |
| optimiser settings | defaults of `PLNnetwork_param()` (`PLNmodels` 1.3.1 in `renv.lock`) |

: `PLNnetwork` settings. Earlier versions of the script passed `control_init` / `control_main`, which `PLNmodels` 1.x no longer accepts; the rewrite uses `control = PLNnetwork_param(...)`. {#tbl-pln-hyperparameters}

```pseudocode
#| label: algo-plnnetwork
#| html-line-number: true
#| pdf-line-number: true

\begin{algorithm}
\caption{PLNnetwork: alternating graphical lasso and variational updates}
\begin{algorithmic}
\Require counts $X$, offsets $O=\log s$, penalty $\lambda$, weights $W$
\State initialise the variational means $M$, variances $S$ and $\Sigma$
\For{$h = 1,\ldots,$ maxit\_out}
  \State $\Omega^{(h)} \gets$ \Call{GraphicalLasso}{$\Sigma^{(h-1)}, \lambda W$}
  \State $(B^{(h)},M^{(h)},S^{(h)}) \gets$ \Call{NLopt}{$B^{(h-1)},M^{(h-1)},S^{(h-1)};\Omega^{(h)}$}
  \State $\Sigma^{(h)} \gets C^{-1}\left[{M^{(h)}}^\top M^{(h)} + \sum_c S_c^{(h)}\right]$
  \State $F_h \gets -\mathrm{ELBO}(B^{(h)},M^{(h)},S^{(h)},\Omega^{(h)}) + \lambda\|\Omega^{(h)}\|_{1,W}$
  \If{$|F_h-F_{h-1}|/|F_h| <$ ftol\_out}
    \State \textbf{break}
  \EndIf
\EndFor
\State \Return $(B,M,S,\Omega,\Sigma)$
\end{algorithmic}
\end{algorithm}
```

@algo-plnnetwork is the block-coordinate scheme of
@chiquetVariationalInferenceSparse2018. The model, the variational
bound and the role of the offset are in
[3.2, PLN](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-2-covariance-network-estimation.html#sec-cov-pln).

The latent moments $(\boldsymbol{\mu}_{z},\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{z})$ are
not on DeCovarT's scale. Given the library $s_c$ of a cell, the moments
of its counts are

$$
\mathbb{E}\,x_{gc}=s_{c}\,e^{\mu_{z,g}+\sigma_{z,gg}/2},
\qquad
\operatorname{Cov}\boldsymbol{x}_{\cdot c}
=
\operatorname{diag}(\mathbb{E}\,\boldsymbol{x}_{\cdot c})
+
\bigl(\mathbb{E}\,\boldsymbol{x}_{\cdot c}\,\mathbb{E}\,\boldsymbol{x}_{\cdot c}^{\top}\bigr)
\circ
\bigl(e^{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{z}}-\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^{\top}\bigr),
$$ {#eq-pln-linear}

with $e^{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{z}}$ taken entrywise. <!-- chk: V3 -->
On raw counts (`normalise = "none"`), `pln_linear_moments(scale = "counts")`
averages @eq-pln-linear over the libraries of the cells being scored,
by the law of total covariance:

$$
\bar{\boldsymbol{x}}=\bar s\,\boldsymbol{m},
\qquad
\operatorname{Cov}\boldsymbol{x}
=
\bar s\operatorname{diag}(\boldsymbol{m})
+\overline{s^{2}}\,(\boldsymbol{m}\boldsymbol{m}^{\top})
\circ\bigl(e^{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{z}}-\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^{\top}\bigr)
+\operatorname{Var}(s)\,\boldsymbol{m}\boldsymbol{m}^{\top},
\qquad
\boldsymbol{m}=e^{\boldsymbol{\mu}_{z}+\operatorname{diag}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{z})/2},
$$ {#eq-pln-linear-avg}

<!-- chk: V3 -->

with $\bar s$, $\overline{s^{2}}$ and $\operatorname{Var}(s)$ the mean,
mean square and variance of those libraries. This is the matrix that
is scored, comparable with the raw sample covariance. The offset
removes every size variation from $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{z}$, biological
size included, so `PLNnetwork` needs no moment correction, only a
choice of what to put back at export. Beside the scored moments, the
driver exports the two brackets without the Poisson diagonal
(`poisson_diag = FALSE`): $\kappa=0$ keeps the depth terms
(`size_term = "keep"`), and the all-technical end gives every cell the
mean library, so $\operatorname{Var}(s)=0$ and
$\overline{s^{2}}=\bar s^{2}$ (`size_term = "drop"`). With
`normalise = "library"` the moments are divided by the size factor
instead (`scale = "normalised"`).

## Cross-validation and outputs {#sec-cov-cv-run}

The same loss selects the tuning parameter of every arm and compares
the five: the held-out Gaussian log-likelihood on the linear scale. For
held-out cells $\mathcal{T}$ and an estimate
$(\widehat{\boldsymbol{\mu}},\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}})$ fitted
without them,

$$
\ell(\widehat{\boldsymbol{\mu}},\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}};\mathcal{T})
=
\frac{1}{|\mathcal{T}|}\sum_{c\in\mathcal{T}}
\log\phi_{G}\bigl(\boldsymbol{x}_{\cdot c};\widehat{\boldsymbol{\mu}},\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}\bigr),
$$ {#eq-heldout-loglik}

computed by `heldout_gaussian_logscore()` through a Cholesky factor of
$\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}$; for the denoised arm,
$\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}$ is @eq-cov-renoise. Why this score is a
legitimate loss for the covariance even though cells are not Gaussian
is in
[3.2, Gaussian log-score](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-2-covariance-network-estimation.html#prp-gaussian-logscore),
and why it replaces AIC, BIC and EBIC as the selector in
[3.2, cross-validation](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-2-covariance-network-estimation.html#sec-cov-cv).

```pseudocode
#| label: algo-cv-covariance
#| html-line-number: true
#| pdf-line-number: true

\begin{algorithm}
\caption{Tuning by K-fold cross-validation, and nested comparison of the five arms}
\begin{algorithmic}
\Procedure{CVSelect}{$X, f, \Lambda, K$}
  \State split the cells of $X$ into $K$ folds at random, with a fixed seed
  \For{$\lambda \in \Lambda$}
    \For{$k = 1,\ldots,K$}
      \State $(\hat\mu,\hat\Sigma) \gets f(X_{-k};\lambda)$
      \State $\ell_k(\lambda) \gets$ \Call{HeldOutLogScore}{$\hat\mu,\hat\Sigma,X_k$}
    \EndFor
    \State $m(\lambda) \gets$ mean of $\ell_k(\lambda)$; $\mathrm{se}(\lambda) \gets$ its standard error
  \EndFor
  \State $\lambda_{\min} \gets \arg\max_{\lambda} m(\lambda)$
  \State $\lambda_{1\mathrm{se}} \gets$ most regularised $\lambda$ with $m(\lambda) \ge m(\lambda_{\min}) - \mathrm{se}(\lambda_{\min})$
  \State \Return $(m, \mathrm{se}, \lambda_{\min}, \lambda_{1\mathrm{se}})$
\EndProcedure
\Procedure{NestedCompare}{$X, \{(f_e,\Lambda_e)\}_{e=1}^{5}, K_{\mathrm{out}}, K_{\mathrm{in}}$}
  \For{$k = 1,\ldots,K_{\mathrm{out}}$}
    \For{$e = 1,\ldots,5$}
      \State $\lambda_e \gets \lambda_{\min}$ of \Call{CVSelect}{$X_{-k}, f_e, \Lambda_e, K_{\mathrm{in}}$}
      \State $(\hat\mu,\hat\Sigma) \gets f_e(X_{-k};\lambda_e)$
      \State $s_{ek} \gets$ \Call{HeldOutLogScore}{$\hat\mu,\hat\Sigma,X_k$}
    \EndFor
  \EndFor
  \State \Return $(s_{ek})$, paired by outer fold
\EndProcedure
\end{algorithmic}
\end{algorithm}
```

Settings in `scripts/03_04_cv_covariance.R`:

- `cv_select_tuning(X, fit_fun, grid, K = 5, seed)` returns the mean and
  standard error per grid value and the `min` and `1se` choices. The
  exported fit uses `min`; `1se` is reported beside it.
- `nested_cv_compare(X, estimators, K_outer = 5, K_inner = 5, seed)` is
  run only to compare the five arms. The inner loop chooses the tuning
  parameter, the outer loop scores the chosen fit on cells it never
  saw. The denoised arm enters with $\kappa=0$; the
  $\hat\kappa_{\max}$ variant is tuned by `cv_select_tuning()` alone
  (@sec-cov-denoised).
- Folds split cells of one unit. The score measures generalisation to
  new cells of this specimen, not to new specimens
  (@nte-pseudoreplication).
- In units with very few cells (29 cells for the somite
  differentiation front, against 5,821 panel genes) each training fold
  has about 23 cells; the shrinkage estimate is the only one expected
  to be stable there.
- **Run time.** At 96 h the panel has 5,821 genes. `SILGGM` (D-S_GL)
  then tests about $1.7\times10^{7}$ gene pairs per unit and
  `PLNnetwork` updates a $5{,}821\times5{,}821$ latent covariance at
  every step, each refitted $K$ times for selection and
  $K_{\mathrm{out}}(K_{\mathrm{in}}+1)$ times for the comparison; these
  two arms dominate the cost. No cap on the panel is imposed to save
  time.

**Diagnostics that are computed but do not select.** The held-out
log-score of @eq-heldout-loglik is the only selector. The diagnostics
of
[3.2, diagnostics](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-2-covariance-network-estimation.html#nte-cov-criteria)
describe a fit; none of them chooses a tuning value or an arm.

- For every arm: the condition number and the eigen-spectrum of
  $\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}_{j}$ against the Marchenko–Pastur band
  of the sample covariance
  [TODO-cite: Marchenko & Pastur 1967; key not in bibliography/REFERENCES.bib]{.highlight};
  the bootstrap spread of $\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}_{j}$ in
  Frobenius and Bures distance (@sec-cov-evaluation); and the
  Hellinger distance and `MixSim` overlap between types
  [@melnykovMixSimPackageSimulating2012] (@sec-cov-plots). Only the
  last two are coded (`gaussian_hellinger()`,
  `gaussian_mixsim_overlap()`); the spectrum and the bootstrap spread
  are planned.
- For the sparse arms only: EBIC along the graphical-lasso path
  (@sec-glasso) and edge stability under subsampling. Both count edges,
  so they do not apply to the shrinkage arms. StARS
  [@liuStabilityApproachRegularization2010] is not run: with 20
  subsamples and 40 penalties it costs about 800 graphical-lasso solves
  per unit, against 40 for the EBIC path.

> For the arm retained for a unit,
$\widehat{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_{\cdot j}$ is the mean of the raw counts of
its cells and $\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}_{j}$ is the selected
covariance, both on the scale of @sec-cov-inputs; @eq-grn-export holds
by construction. For `PLNnetwork` both come from @eq-pln-linear-avg;
for the denoised arm the exported covariance is
$\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}^{\mathrm{bio}}_{j}$. Which covariance
layer these cell-level moments identify, and how the sample scales are
estimated inside the DeCovarT fit, is in
[2.1, three regimes](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/02-1-single-cell-generative-optimisation.html#sec-three-regimes)
and
[2.1, profile Newton](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/02-1-single-cell-generative-optimisation.html#sec-profile-newton).

### Displays {#sec-cov-plots}

Plot functions are in `R/plot_grn_regularisation.R`. Each display
answers one question.

**Choosing the tuning parameter (one unit, one arm).**

- Cross-validation curve: $m(\lambda)\pm\mathrm{se}(\lambda)$ against
  the tuning parameter, with the `min` and `1se` choices marked
  (new; not produced yet).
- Regularisation path: each off-diagonal entry of
  $\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Omega}}(\lambda)$ against $\log\lambda$,
  five edges that survive at the selected $\lambda$ and five that are
  driven to zero (graphical lasso, `PLNnetwork`).
- EBIC against $\log\lambda$, and EBIC against edge density
  $|E|/\{G(G-1)/2\}$ (diagnostic only).

**Comparing arms (one unit).**

- Outer-fold held-out scores $s_{ek}$ of @algo-cv-covariance, one line
  per fold across the five arms, so that the comparison is paired.
- Partial-correlation heatmaps at the selected tuning parameter, with
  one gene order frozen across estimators and types,
  $$
  \rho_{gg'\mid\mathrm{rest}}
  =
  -\frac{\omega_{gg'}}{\sqrt{\omega_{gg}\omega_{g'g'}}},
  $$ {#eq-partial}
  on a diverging scale centred at zero.
- For the three sparse estimators: UpSet plots of edge presence and of
  signed edges.

**Comparing types (one time).** Pairwise Hellinger distance and
`MixSim` overlap between the exported Gaussians on the linear scale
(`gaussian_hellinger()`, `gaussian_mixsim_overlap()` in
`R/ebic_regularisation_path.R`). Distances computed on another scale
(nonparanormal scores, $\log(1+x)$) do not describe what DeCovarT has
to separate.

### Evaluation {#sec-cov-evaluation}

There is no ground-truth network for murine gastruloids, and the
estimand is a covariance. The scores are therefore relative, in this
order of weight:

1. **Held-out likelihood**, outer folds of @algo-cv-covariance: the
   selector, and the only score that compares all five arms on one
   scale.
2. **Downstream deconvolution**: DeCovarT error on the matched 48 h
   bulk and in the misspecification sweep of @sec-sensitivity, with
   $\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}_{j}$ from each arm. This is the
   score tied to the paper's estimand.
3. **Technical stability**: a bootstrap of cells within type, labels
   fixed (@nte-pseudoreplication). Edge-inclusion frequencies for the
   sparse estimators and the Frobenius spread of
   $\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}_{j}$ for every arm. Conditional on
   this specimen.
4. **Separation of types**: Hellinger and `MixSim` overlap of
   @sec-cov-plots.
5. **Concordance of the sparse estimators**: overlap of edge sets
   (intersection over the smaller set) and Hamming distance between
   skeletons, raw and divided by $G(G-1)/2$. Agreement is a robustness
   number, not a validation.

Scores that need a known skeleton, curated transcription-factor
targets, other assays or perturbations are perspectives
([3.2, perspectives](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-2-covariance-network-estimation.html#sec-cov-perspectives)).
